02-zweihand.title: Two-hand control
02-zweihand.mail.subject: Press 7 – safety circuit
02-zweihand.mail.body:
Good day,

after last week's accident the trade association shut down our press 7. The operators had taped one of the two buttons down to keep a hand free. That must never be possible again.

We need a real two-hand control: both buttons have to be pressed within half a second, and after every stroke both have to be released again.

The details are in the datasheet. Please test thoroughly – fingers are at stake.

Kind regards
Konrad Ulmer
Plant management
02-zweihand.datasheet:
# Press 7 – two-hand control

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Left button, normally open |
| S2 | DI | Right button, normally open |
| Y1 | DO | Press valve, 1 = ram moves |

## Function

1. **Y1** may only be switched on while **both** buttons are pressed.
2. The second button must be pressed **within 0.5 s** after the first. Otherwise the press stays off until both buttons have been released.
3. If a button is released, Y1 drops out immediately. Pressing only that button again does **not** restart the press – first **both** buttons must be released.
4. The order of the buttons does not matter.

## Timing

Y1 must react no later than 15 ms after the second button press or after releasing.

## Note

Timers need an instance DB, e.g. `"Fenster"` of type `IEC_TIMER`, called with `"Fenster".TON(IN := …, PT := T#500ms);`. States that must persist over several cycles belong in a global DB.

03-stromstoss.title: Impulse switch with bouncing button
03-stromstoss.mail.subject: Corridor light acting up
03-stromstoss.mail.body:
Hi all,

in the office building Am Wehr we replaced the old impulse relays with a small controller. Since then the tenants complain: sometimes the light goes on when pressed and immediately off again, sometimes nothing happens at all.

I suspect the old buttons – they bounce like crazy. One press on, one press off, that's all anyone wants. Could you solve this cleanly?

Thanks and best regards
Mara Lindner
03-stromstoss.datasheet:
# Corridor light Am Wehr

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Light button, normally open, **bounces** |
| H1 | DO | Corridor lighting, 1 = on |

## Bouncing of S1

When pressed and released, the contact switches 2 to 6 extra times, 1 to 5 ms apart. After that the signal is stable.

## Function

1. Every press of **S1** toggles **H1** (on → off → on …).
2. Releasing the button changes nothing.
3. One press must toggle **exactly once** – bouncing must not cause extra toggles.

## Timing

The lamp should toggle **15 to 65 ms** after the press. Faster is not possible without falling for the bounce.

## Note

A proven approach: only treat the signal as pressed once it has been stable for a certain time (on-delay), then evaluate the rising edge (`R_TRIG`).

04-ampel.title: Roadworks traffic light
04-ampel.mail.subject: Traffic light for the bridge repair
04-ampel.mail.body:
Hello,

from Monday we are repairing the Mühlbach bridge, traffic runs in a single lane. Our rented traffic light is broken, and until a replacement arrives we need our own controller.

The sequence is the usual: red, red-amber, green, amber, red again. The times are in the datasheet. The key switch turns the light on and off. When switched on it must always start with red.

Best regards
Bernd Aigner
Civil engineering
04-ampel.datasheet:
# Roadworks traffic light

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Key switch “Operation” (1 = on) |
| H1 | DO | Red |
| H2 | DO | Amber |
| H3 | DO | Green |

## Sequence (repeats while S1 = 1)

| Phase | Duration | Red | Amber | Green |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Red | 3 s | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Red-amber | 1 s | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Green | 3 s | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| Amber | 1 s | 0 | 1 | 0 |

## Function

1. With S1 = 1 the sequence starts with the phase **red**.
2. With S1 = 0 all lamps are off immediately.
3. Switching on again starts at red again.

## Timing

Switching times may deviate by at most ±60 ms.

## Note

A single timer for the whole cycle is enough: the elapsed time `ET` can be compared with time constants, e.g. `"Takt".ET < T#3s`.

05-zaehler.title: Part counter with light barrier
05-zaehler.mail.subject: Boxes are shipped half empty
05-zaehler.mail.body:
Good morning,

on line 2 the parts drop from the belt into a box. After five parts a lamp should light up so the operator swaps the box and acknowledges.

But the old controller often reports “full” after just two or three parts. I looked at the light barrier: when a part passes, the signal flutters at the edges. Please program it so that every part counts exactly once.

Kind regards
Sabine Brandl
05-zaehler.datasheet:
# Line 2 – box counter

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | DI | Light barrier, 1 = part in the beam (approx. 100 ms per part), **flutters** at the edges |
| S1 | DI | Button “Acknowledge”, normally open |
| H1 | DO | Lamp “Box full” |

## Fluttering of B1

When a part enters and leaves, the signal switches 2 to 8 extra times, 1 to 3 ms apart.

## Function

1. Every part counts exactly once.
2. After the **5th part** H1 lights up.
3. **S1** resets the counter to 0 and clears H1 – even if the box was not full yet.

## Timing

H1 should come on **0 to 70 ms** after the 5th part enters; after S1 off immediately.

## Note

Counters need an instance DB, e.g. of type `CTU_INT` or `IEC_COUNTER`.

06-stern-dreieck.title: Star-delta starting
06-stern-dreieck.mail.subject: Fuse blows when starting
06-stern-dreieck.mail.body:
Hi,

our big fan motor is started in star-delta so the inrush current doesn't blow the fuse. Since the conversion there's a bang every now and then when switching over – the electrician says the star and delta contactors were briefly closed at the same time. That's a short circuit!

Please build a controller that reliably prevents it. The contactors don't switch instantly, that's in the datasheet of the relay module.

Greetings from the mill
Jakob Ostertag
06-stern-dreieck.datasheet:
# Fan – star-delta starting

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Button “Start”, normally open |
| S2 | DI | Button “Stop”, **normally closed** |
| K1 | DO | Mains contactor – **power output** |
| K2 | DO | Star contactor – **power output** |
| K3 | DO | Delta contactor – **power output** |

Contactors must be driven via a **relay module (REL 4)**. Its contacts close 15 ms after the command and only open 30 ms after it.

## Sequence

1. **Start:** K1 and K2 on (star operation).
2. After **2 s**: K2 off.
3. **Changeover pause** of at least 50 ms, at most 200 ms.
4. K3 on (delta operation), K1 stays on.
5. **Stop** (or a wire break at S2) switches everything off immediately. Stop has priority over start.

## Safety

**K2 and K3 must never be closed at the same time** – not even for a millisecond.

checks.Dreieckbetrieb nach max. 200 ms Pause: Delta operation after at most 200 ms pause
checks.Kein Dreieck vor Ablauf der Sternzeit: No delta before the star time has elapsed
checks.Stern- und Dreieckschütz nie gleichzeiti: Star and delta contactor never at the same time

07-tank.title: Elevated tank with level control
07-tank.mail.subject: Pump is switching itself to death
07-tank.mail.body:
Hello,

the Talgrund elevated tank is filled by a pump from the well. The level probe delivers an analog signal. Our current controller switches the pump on and off at 60 % – and because the signal jitters a little, it switches dozens of times a minute there. The second pump this year is already broken.

Please: pump on below 40 %, off above 80 %. In between it should simply stay as it is.

Best regards
Petra Wendlinger
Network operations
07-tank.datasheet:
# Elevated tank Talgrund

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | AI | Level probe 0…100 % → 0…27648, **noisy** (± approx. 0.3 %) |
| P1 | DO | Well pump – **power output** (via REL 4) |

## Plant

The pump fills at 12 %/s, consumption draws 2 to 9 %/s depending on the time of day. Initial level 50 %.

## Function (two-point control with hysteresis)

1. Level **below 40 %** → pump on.
2. Level **above 80 %** → pump off.
3. In between the pump keeps its state.

## Verification

- The level stays between 35 % and 85 %.
- The pump switches at most 10 times per test.

## Note

Raw value in percent: `NORM_X(MIN := 0, VALUE := "Fuellstand", MAX := 27648)` gives 0.0…1.0, `SCALE_X` scales to 0.0…100.0.

08-drahtbruch.title: Wire break at the temperature sensor
08-drahtbruch.mail.subject: Drying oven – almost burned down
08-drahtbruch.mail.body:
Hello,

last night the cable to the temperature sensor of the drying oven chafed through. The controller read a nonsense value and kept the heating running. Luckily the over-temperature switch tripped.

We need a temperature control that detects a sensor fault, then immediately switches off the heating and sets a fault lamp. The lamp should only go out once someone has acknowledged and the sensor is fine again.

Regards
Tobias Seidel
08-drahtbruch.datasheet:
# Drying oven – temperature control

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | AI | Temperature sensor 0…150 °C → 0…27648 |
| S1 | DI | Button “Acknowledge”, normally open |
| K1 | DO | Heating contactor – **power output** (via REL 4) |
| H1 | DO | Fault lamp |

## Sensor faults

On **wire break** or **overflow** the module delivers the raw value **32767**, on **underflow** **−32768**. Valid values lie between −4864 and 32511.

## Function

1. **Control:** below 60 °C heating on, above 65 °C heating off, unchanged in between.
2. **Sensor fault:** substitute reaction “heating **off**” (safe state), **H1 on**.
3. When the fault ends, the heating controls normally again right away.
4. **H1** stays on until **S1** is pressed **and** no fault is present any more.

## Timing

Deviation at most ±40 ms. Mind the relay switching times (on 15 ms, off 30 ms).

09-mittelwert.title: Calm display for a restless value
09-mittelwert.mail.subject: Flow display jumps around
09-mittelwert.mail.body:
Hello,

in the brewhouse the flow display at the wort cooler jumps so wildly that nobody can read what is really flowing. The manufacturer says the noise comes from the flow and is normal – you just have to smooth the value.

Can you condition the analog signal so the display is calm but still follows the real flow?

Cheers and thanks!
Lena Kranz
09-mittelwert.datasheet:
# Brewhouse – flow display

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | AI | Flow meter 0…100 m³/h → 0…27648, **very noisy** (standard deviation approx. 900 digits) |
| A1 | AO | Display 0…100 m³/h ← 0…27648 |

## Function

A1 shows the **smoothed** measured value. The display may deviate from the true flow by at most **±1200 digits** (approx. 4 m³/h) – from 0.5 s after the start.

## Notes

- **Moving average:** mean of the last n values.
- **Exponential average** (simpler, no buffer): `y := y + (x − y) / n` in every cycle. A larger n smooths more but reacts more slowly.
- Keep intermediate values as `Real` in a global DB; for output `REAL_TO_INT`.

10-bohrstation.title: Drilling station as a sequence
10-bohrstation.mail.subject: Drilling station – please as a step sequence
10-bohrstation.mail.body:
Hello,

our drilling station should finally run automatically: insert the workpiece, press start, done. The last attempt was a tangle of memory bits, and the drill got stuck in the material twice.

Please make it a clean step sequence – one step after the other, each with a clear condition to move on. The order is in the datasheet.

Regards
Jonas Ostermann
10-bohrstation.datasheet:
# Drilling station BS-2

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Start button |
| B1 | DI | Drill up (end position) |
| B2 | DI | Drill down (drilling depth reached) |
| B3 | DI | Workpiece clamped |
| Y1 | DO | Clamping cylinder (1 = clamp) |
| M1 | DO | Drill motor – **power output** (via REL 4) |
| Y2 | DO | Feed down |
| Y3 | DO | Feed up |

## Sequence

| Step | Activity | next when |
|---|---|---|
| 0 Home | everything off | start **pressed** (edge) and drill up |
| 1 Clamp | Y1 | workpiece clamped (B3) |
| 2 Drill | Y1, M1, Y2 | drilling depth reached (B2) |
| 3 Dwell | Y1, M1 | at least **250 ms** at the bottom |
| 4 Lift | Y1, M1, Y3 | drill up (B1) |
| 5 Release | everything off | workpiece no longer clamped (B3 = 0) |

## Mechanics

Clamping takes 150 ms, lowering 1 s, lifting 0.5 s. From 60 % depth the drill is inside the workpiece: there the workpiece must be clamped and the motor running, otherwise there is **damage**. Lowering and lifting at the same time jams the feed.

## Note

Step number in a data block (Int), advance with `CASE … OF`, then derive the outputs from the step number. Alternatively write the sequence in a function block in **GRAPH**.

checks.Festhalten von Start löst keinen neuen A: Holding start does not trigger a new cycle
checks.Kein Schaden an Bohrer oder Werkstück: No damage to drill or workpiece
checks.Senken und Heben nie gleichzeitig: Lowering and lifting never at the same time

11-sortierweiche.title: Sorting diverter by height
11-sortierweiche.mail.subject: Tall parcels end up on the wrong chute
11-sortierweiche.mail.body:
Hi,

on the sorting belt we measure the parcel height at the first light barrier. The diverter, however, sits almost a metre further on. As long as there's only one parcel on the track everything works – but when it gets busy, the diverter is set for the parcel that was just measured, not for the one that is just arriving.

So the controller has to remember what is on its way. Can you manage that?

Aylin Karaca
Engineering
11-sortierweiche.datasheet:
# Sorting track SW-1

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | DI | Light barrier at the measuring point (1 = parcel present) |
| B2 | AI | Height sensor above B1, 0…300 mm → 0…27648, slightly noisy |
| B3 | DI | Light barrier before the diverter |
| Y1 | DO | Diverter (1 = tall parcels to the side) |

## Track

The belt always runs. A parcel needs **900 ms** from B1 to B3 and occupies a light barrier for 250 ms. Parcels follow at least 350 ms apart – so three or more can be on the way at the same time.

## Function

- Parcels **taller than 120 mm** go to the side (Y1 = 1), lower ones straight on (Y1 = 0).
- What counts is the diverter position at the moment the parcel **leaves** B3.
- Measuring happens while the parcel is in B1.

## Note

Parcels don't overtake each other. A queue of bits fits in a Word: `SHL`/`SHR` shift, `AND`/`OR` set and read.

12-pwm.title: Heating band in cycles
12-pwm.mail.subject: Heating band stepless – but only with a switching output
12-pwm.mail.body:
Hello,

the heating band at the extruder nozzle hangs on a solid-state relay that can only do on/off. We still want to set the power with the potentiometer: 0 to 100 %.

The idea: switch on every second and off again sooner or later depending on the setpoint. Unfortunately there's no analog output.

Best regards
Moritz Lindauer
12-pwm.datasheet:
# Nozzle heating DH-3

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Enable (switch) |
| B1 | AI | Power potentiometer 0…100 % → 0…27648 |
| E1 | DO | Solid-state relay heating band |

## Function (pulse width modulation)

- Period **1 s**.
- In every period E1 is on for as long as the setpoint says: 30 % → 300 ms on, 700 ms off.
- Without enable E1 stays off.

## Verification

In every one-second window the on-share must be accurate to **3 percentage points**. The window right after a setpoint change is not evaluated.

## Note

A timer that restarts itself (`IN := NOT Q`) gives, via `ET`, a running time within the period. `TIME_TO_DINT` converts it to milliseconds.

13-koppel.title: Pump house and control room
13-koppel.mail.subject: Two cabinets, one pump
13-koppel.mail.body:
Good day,

the controls for the waste-water pump are in the control room, the pump itself in the pump house next door. Between them is a fire wall – no cables may pass. Only the bus cable between two coupler modules is allowed.

So: one CPU per side, and the two have to talk to each other. Details in the datasheet.

Kind regards
I. Kowalczyk
13-koppel.datasheet:
# Pumping station Rabenfeld

## Field devices

| Device | Side | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Control room | DI | Pump on (switch) |
| S2 | Control room | DI | Acknowledge (button) |
| H1 | Control room | DO | Lamp running |
| H2 | Control room | DO | Lamp fault |
| B1 | Pump house | DI | Motor protection – **normally closed** (1 = OK) |
| K1 | Pump house | DO | Pump contactor – **power output** (via REL 4) |

## Cabinet

There is a **partition** in the middle: no module on it, no cable through it. Each side needs its own CPU. A **coupler module (KOP)** per CPU connects the two: what one CPU writes to %QW100 and %QW102, the other reads in %IW100 and %IW102 – from its next cycle. Single bits work too: %Q100.0 arrives as %I100.0.

## Function

1. The pump runs while S1 is on and no fault is present.
2. If the motor protection trips (B1 = 0), a **fault is latched**: pump off, H2 on.
3. S2 clears the fault – but only once the motor protection is OK again.
4. H1 shows that the pump is switched on.

tests.aus: Fault with the pump switched off

14-impulse.title: Filling by pulses
14-impulse.mail.subject: Bottles overflow
14-impulse.mail.body:
Hello,

our flow meter gives one pulse per tenth of a litre – very short, only 2 ms. Filling should close after 120 pulses. But our controller counts too few and the bottles overflow.

The dealer said we'd need an “interrupt-capable input card”. We're not allowed to use a faster CPU, the medium one is mandatory.

Best regards
Greta Hagedorn
14-impulse.datasheet:
# Filling AF-120

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Start filling (button) |
| B1 | DI | Flow meter: **2 ms pulse** per 0.1 l, 9…22 ms apart |
| Y1 | DO | Filling valve |

## Function

1. Start opens the valve and starts counting at 0.
2. At the **120th pulse** the valve closes (no later than 30 ms after it).

## Hardware

Only the **CPU mittel** (5 ms cycle) is permitted – a pulse is shorter than its cycle. The **DI 8 HF** input card can trigger a **hardware interrupt** on every edge: the CPU then interrupts immediately and runs an interrupt OB (OB40). Its channel 0 can alternatively count pulses as a **high-speed counter**.

## Note

Create an OB of type *hardware interrupt* in the block tree and set input and edge. The interrupt OB counts, OB1 controls the valve. Both share a data block.

15-pi-regler.title: Temperature control for the hardening furnace
15-pi-regler.mail.subject: Furnace never reaches the temperature
15-pi-regler.mail.body:
Hi,

our tempering furnace always stays a few degrees below the setpoint. If you turn the gain up, it starts to oscillate. A colleague said we're missing the integral part.

Can you build us a PI controller? The furnace reacts sluggishly and with a delay, details in the datasheet.

Felix Brandtner
15-pi-regler.datasheet:
# Tempering furnace AO-200

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | AI | Furnace temperature 0…200 °C → 0…27648, noisy |
| B2 | AI | Setpoint adjuster 0…200 °C |
| E1 | AO | Heating power 0…100 % → 0…27648 |

## Process

First-order lag with dead time: 100 % heating power results in 20 °C + 180 °C in the steady state. Time constant **6 s**, dead time **1.5 s**. Without heating the furnace cools down to 20 °C. Opening the door loses up to 25 °C.

## Requirement

- After settling **± 2 °C** around the setpoint.
- At most 8 °C overshoot.

## Note (PI controller)

`y = Kp · (e + 1/Ti · ∫e dt)` with e = setpoint − actual. Starting values: Kp = 1.5 %/°C, Ti = 5 s. Sample evenly: a **cyclic interrupt OB** (e.g. OB30, every 100 ms) calls the controller; an own **FB** “PI” keeps the integral in its static data. Limit the output to 0…100 % and then stop integrating (anti-windup).

16-zwei-behaelter.title: Two tanks, one controller
16-zwei-behaelter.mail.subject: New level probes – and nobody notices the cable break
16-zwei-behaelter.mail.body:
Hello,

we installed new 4–20 mA level probes in both supply tanks. The pumps should refill as before, each tank on its own.

The real reason for the change: last month a probe cable was torn off, the old controller read 0 % and kept the pump running until the tank overflowed. With 4–20 mA that should no longer happen.

Regards
Lena Kaltenecker
16-zwei-behaelter.datasheet:
# Supply tanks VB-1 and VB-2

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | AI | Level VB-1, 0…100 %, **4–20 mA** |
| B2 | AI | Level VB-2, 0…100 %, **4–20 mA** |
| P1 | DO | Pump VB-1 – power output (via REL 4) |
| P2 | DO | Pump VB-2 – power output (via REL 4) |
| H1 | DO | Lamp fault |

## Function per tank

1. Level **below 40 %** → pump on.
2. Level **above 80 %** → pump off.
3. **Wire break** of the probe (raw value 32767) → pump off immediately, H1 on while the fault is present.

## Analog inputs

Analog channels are set to **0–10 V** by default. A 4–20 mA probe on a 0–10 V channel only delivers overflow. The measuring range is set on the plugged-in module (click the module). Only in the 4–20 mA range does the channel detect a wire break.

## Note

Both tanks behave the same – an own function (FC), called twice, saves statements.

checks.P1 aus während des Kabelbruchs: P1 off during the cable break

17-frequenzumrichter.title: Conveyor on a frequency inverter
17-frequenzumrichter.mail.subject: Belt knocks the boxes over when starting
17-frequenzumrichter.mail.body:
Hello,

our feed belt now hangs on a frequency inverter. Unfortunately the inverter does exactly what it's told: if the setpoint jumps, the belt jumps – and the boxes fall over.

The operator sets the speed with the potentiometer. The controller should ramp up and down smoothly and report when the belt has reached its speed. The feedback comes from the inverter.

Tomasz Nowak
17-frequenzumrichter.datasheet:
# Feed belt ZB-3

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Belt on (switch) |
| B1 | AI | Speed potentiometer 0…100 %, **0–10 V** |
| H1 | DO | Lamp “Speed reached” |
| K1 | DO | Inverter enable |
| A1 | AO | Frequency setpoint 0…50 Hz, **0–10 V** |
| B2 | AI | Actual frequency from the inverter 0…50 Hz, **4–20 mA** |

## Function

1. Potentiometer 0…100 % corresponds to 0…50 Hz.
2. With S1 on: K1 on, the setpoint at A1 ramps at **10 Hz/s** to the potentiometer value.
3. S1 off: the setpoint ramps at 10 Hz/s to 0, then K1 off.
4. H1 lights up when S1 is on and the **actual frequency** (B2) matches the potentiometer value to within 1 Hz.

## Inverter

The inverter has no ramp of its own. If the frequency changes faster than **15 Hz/s**, the boxes tip over (overload). Without enable the belt coasts down.

## Note

OB1 runs at the CPU's fixed cycle. With a 10 ms cycle, 10 Hz/s is exactly 0.1 Hz per cycle – a faster CPU needs a smaller step. Analog channels are set to 0–10 V by default.

18-lackmischer.title: Paint mixer with recipes
18-lackmischer.mail.subject: Three recipes, one mixer – and the power keeps failing
18-lackmischer.mail.body:
Good day,

our mixer doses base paint and hardener into a vessel and then stirs. We run three recipes; the operator chooses the current one with three buttons.

The old controller has two quirks: if someone picks another recipe during a mix, it changes the times in the middle of the sequence. And after every power failure – we have a few of those in winter – it is back on recipe 1, even if the whole shift runs recipe 3.

Please store the recipe data cleanly as a table, we want to add more recipes later.

Thanks and kind regards
Theresa Oberhuber
18-lackmischer.datasheet:
# Mixer M2 – recipe control

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Button “Recipe 1”, normally open |
| S2 | DI | Button “Recipe 2”, normally open |
| S3 | DI | Button “Recipe 3”, normally open |
| S4 | DI | Button “Start”, normally open |
| Y1 | DO | Valve base paint |
| Y2 | DO | Valve hardener |
| M1 | DO | Stirrer |

## Recipes

| Recipe | Base paint (Y1) | Hardener (Y2) | Stirring (M1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.0 s | 1.0 s | 3.0 s |
| 2 | 1.0 s | 2.5 s | 2.0 s |
| 3 | 3.0 s | – | 4.0 s |

## Sequence

1. S1 … S3 choose the recipe, at any time. Without a choice **recipe 1** applies.
2. **Start** (S4, rising edge) begins a mix with the chosen recipe: first Y1, then Y2, then M1 – each for the time from the table, back to back. A recipe without hardener skips Y2.
3. During a mix neither start nor a new choice affects the running sequence; the choice applies from the next mix.
4. **Power failure**: the mix aborts, all outputs are off. After power returns nothing continues until start is pressed. The **chosen recipe is kept**.

## Timing

Tolerance ± 50 ms per switching edge.

## Notes

- A PLC data type `"Rezept"` with three times and a global DB with `Array[1..3] of "Rezept"` hold the table; at start take a copy of the chosen recipe.
- Whatever should survive a power failure must be **retentive** (column “Retain”). Start values for the table can also be set in the **startup OB (OB100)**.

tests.stromausfall: Power failure in the middle of recipe 3

19-schichtbuch.title: Shift log for fault messages
19-schichtbuch.mail.subject: When exactly did the extruder fail?
19-schichtbuch.mail.body:
Hello,

on the film line there are two fault signals: extruder and cooling. So far only a common fault lamp lights up, and at the end of the shift nobody knows what happened when.

We'd like a small shift log in the controller: the last five messages with the time as text, so the control room can display them directly. It is cleared at the shift handover. And please make sure a power failure doesn't empty the log – that's exactly when we need it most.

Best regards
Milan Petrov
19-schichtbuch.datasheet:
# Film line 1 – shift log

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | DI | Extruder fault, 1 = fault |
| B2 | DI | Cooling fault, 1 = fault |
| S1 | DI | Button “Shift handover”, normally open |
| H1 | DO | Common fault lamp |

## Function

1. H1 is lit while B1 or B2 report a fault.
2. Every **new** fault (rising edge at B1 or B2) creates an entry with the controller's time (`RD_SYS_T`) in the format `hh:mm:ss Extruder` or `hh:mm:ss Kuehlung`, two digits with a leading zero, e.g. `06:00:02 Extruder`.
3. Entries are stored in **`"Schichtbuch".Eintrag`** – `Array[0..4] of String[20]` – as a **ring buffer**: the n-th entry since the handover (counted from 0) goes into `Eintrag[n MOD 5]`, so the sixth overwrites `Eintrag[0]`. **`"Schichtbuch".Anzahl`** (Int) counts the entries since the handover.
4. **S1** clears all entries (empty text) and sets Anzahl to 0.
5. The shift log survives a **power failure**.

## Verification

The check reads `"Schichtbuch".Eintrag[0]` … `[4]` and `"Schichtbuch".Anzahl` at the end of every test case – the names must be exactly these. The controller clock starts every test on Monday, 5 January 2026, at 06:00:00.

## Notes

- `RD_SYS_T(OUT => #jetzt);` with `#jetzt : DTL` gives hour, minute and second (`#jetzt.HOUR` …, type USInt).
- `USINT_TO_STRING`, `CONCAT` and a small FC with a return value for the leading zero save typing.

20-kuehlpumpe.title: Cooling pump with fallback mode
20-kuehlpumpe.mail.subject: Mould overheated because the measurement was gone
20-kuehlpumpe.mail.body:
Hello,

our mould cooling switches the pump according to the water temperature. Last week the measuring module failed – the controller then read 0 °C, switched the pump off and the mould overheated. A wire break at the sensor does exactly the same.

If the measurement isn't right, the pump should simply keep running and a fault lamp should come on. When the measurement returns, normal operation continues. And please don't go to STOP – that would be the worst.

Regards
Jonas Haselbach
20-kuehlpumpe.datasheet:
# Mould cooling K3

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | AI | Water temperature 0 … 100 °C (raw value 0 … 27648) |
| M1 | DO | Cooling pump |
| H1 | DO | Fault lamp “Measurement faulty” |

## Function

1. Normal operation: pump **on from 60 °C**, **off below 50 °C**, in between the state stays.
2. **Measurement faulty** – wire break (raw value 32767) or **measuring module failed**: the pump runs continuously (fallback mode), H1 is lit.
3. Once the measurement is OK again, normal operation applies immediately, H1 goes out.
4. The CPU must never go to STOP.

## Timing

Tolerance ± 50 ms per switching edge.

## Notes

- A failed module delivers 0 – that looks like 0 °C. Only the **rack failure OB (OB86)** reports the failure: `#Event_Class = 16#39` coming, `16#38` going.
- A wire break can be detected from the raw value or via the module's **diagnostics** and the **diagnostic interrupt OB (OB82)**.
- Without an error OB the CPU stays in RUN on a module failure – but it doesn't notice either.

21-ruhige-anzeige.title: Calm display without cycle time errors
21-ruhige-anzeige.mail.subject: The new averaging brings the controller to a halt
21-ruhige-anzeige.mail.body:
Hello,

the flow meter at the filling line is very noisy. Our working student programmed a moving average over the last four seconds – the display is calm, but after a few seconds the CPU goes to STOP with “cycle time exceeded”.

Please solve it so the display stays calm but follows a jump within four and a half seconds at the latest – and the controller keeps running.

Best regards
Petra Steinberger
21-ruhige-anzeige.datasheet:
# Filling L2 – flow display

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | AI | Flow 0 … 100 m³/h, **very noisy** |
| A1 | AO | Display 0 … 100 m³/h (same raw range as B1) |

## Function

1. A1 shows the **moving average of the last 800 values** (with a 5 ms cycle: 4 s).
2. Deviation from the true flow at most **± 800** raw units once the window is full (from 4.5 s after start or after a jump).
3. The CPU must not go to STOP.

## Notes

- The medium CPU manages **2000 instructions per cycle**. A loop over 800 values in every cycle needs several times that.
- A moving average can be updated continuously: add the new value to the sum, subtract the oldest. Alternatively spread the work over several cycles.
- 800 values take 1600 bytes – more than the small CPU has in work memory.
- A **time error OB (OB80)** tolerates a single overrun, but not a permanent one.

22-ofen-pid.title: Furnace control with PID_Compact
22-ofen-pid.mail.subject: Every time someone opens the door …
22-ofen-pid.mail.body:
Hello,

our stoving furnace should hold a fixed temperature. The old controller was home-made and had to be re-tuned after every modification. This time please use the ready-made PID block – supposedly it can tune itself.

The actual problem is the loading door: when it is open the temperature drops, and by the time the controller notices, the batch is ruined. Can't you see what's coming from the door contact?

Best regards
Lena Kofler
22-ofen-pid.datasheet:
# Stoving furnace E2

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | AI | Furnace temperature 0 … 300 °C (raw value 0 … 27648), slightly noisy |
| B2 | AI | Setpoint adjuster 0 … 300 °C |
| S1 | DI | Door contact: 1 = loading door open |
| E1 | AO | Heating power 0 … 100 % (raw value 0 … 27648) |

## Process

- Full heating power raises the temperature by **300 °C** above ambient (20 °C).
- Time constant **20 s**, dead time **2 s** between heating and measurement.
- Open door: **50 °C** heat loss, effective immediately. Compensating it needs about **17 %** more heating power.

## Requirements

1. Heat up to the setpoint without overshooting above **setpoint + 8 °C**.
2. From 80 s after the start: temperature **± 4 °C** around the setpoint.
3. Also while the door is open and afterwards: **± 6 °C**.

## Notes

- **PID_Compact** (technology): create an instance DB, start values Gain, Ti in the Data blocks tab. Self-tuning (Tune) shows suitable values – but it takes longer than a test.
- Rules of thumb for this process: Gain ≈ 1.3, Ti ≈ 18 s.
- **Feedforward**: if the cause of a disturbance can be measured (door contact), the program can adjust the output immediately instead of waiting for the control error.

checks.180 °C ± 6 °C mit offener Tür und danach: 180 °C ± 6 °C with the door open and afterwards

23-positionieren.title: Positioning with a high-speed counter
23-positionieren.mail.subject: The saw always cuts too long
23-positionieren.mail.body:
Hello,

the stop on our cross-cut saw moves with an incremental encoder. The old program counts the pulses in the cycle – and at rapid speed apparently more pulses arrive than the controller notices. The boards come out too long every time.

Please make the stop move exactly 400 mm further on every start. Exactly means: to within one millimetre.

Thanks and regards
Martin Stöckl
23-positionieren.datasheet:
# Stop A1 on the cross-cut saw

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Start button |
| B1 | DI | Incremental encoder, **2 pulses per mm** |
| M1 | DO | Drive rapid speed (200 mm/s) |
| M2 | DO | Drive creep speed (20 mm/s) |

## Mechanics

- The stop is at 0 mm when switched on.
- Accelerating and braking at **1000 mm/s²**: from rapid speed the drive needs 20 mm to reach creep speed, from creep speed 0.2 mm to stand still.
- If M1 is on, rapid speed applies (M2 doesn't matter); only M2: creep speed.

## Function

1. Every rising edge at S1 moves the target by **400 mm** (targets 400, 800, …).
2. The stop starts at rapid speed, switches to creep speed in time and stops at the target **± 1 mm**.

## Notes

- At rapid speed 400 pulses arrive per second – one every 2.5 ms. In the cycle the CPU only sees every second to fourth one.
- The **DI 8 HF** counts every edge itself at channel 0 as a **high-speed counter (HSC)** (control cabinet: click the module). Count value in `%ID112`, handbook “Technology”.

24-pumpstation.title: Pumping station with operator panel
24-pumpstation.mail.subject: New pumping station – without cables across the site
24-pumpstation.mail.body:
Hello,

the new pumping station is 200 m away from the operations building. We don't want to run control cables there: in the station there is only a distributed I/O station on the network, the CPU stays in the operations building.

Operation is via the new panel: start, stop, running and fault indication. If the connection to the station breaks or the motor protection trips, we want to see an alarm on the panel – and the pump must not restart on its own afterwards.

Regards
Andreas Gruber
24-pumpstation.datasheet:
# Pumping station PS 4

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Location | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | DI | Station | Motor protection: 1 = OK, 0 = tripped |
| K1 | DO | Station | Pump contactor (power: relay output) |
| P1 | Panel | – | Start button |
| P2 | Panel | – | Stop button |
| P3 | Panel | – | Lamp running |
| P4 | Panel | – | Lamp motor protection fault |
| P5 | Panel | – | Lamp station failed |

## Layout

- The station is to the right of the partition. Cables don't pass through the wall: there sits an **interface module IM PN** with the I/O modules, the CPU stays on the left.
- The panel is connected via memory bits (tags P_Start, P_Stopp, P_Betrieb, P_Motorschutz, P_Station).

## Function

1. Start (P1) switches the pump on, stop (P2) off. P3 shows operation.
2. **Fault**: motor protection tripped **or station failed** → pump off, an **alarm** (Program_Alarm) is active as long as the fault lasts.
3. The lamps tell the cause apart: P4 only when the motor protection tripped, P5 only when the station failed.
4. Once the fault is over, the pump stays off until start is pressed again; the lamp goes out with the fault.
5. The CPU must not go to STOP.

## Timing

Tolerance ± 100 ms (update time, panel refresh cycle).

## Notes

- The **rack failure OB (OB86)** reports the station failure with `#Event_Class` 16#39 (coming) or 16#38 (going).
- While the station has failed, the CPU reads the motor protection as 0 – without OB86 a station failure looks like a tripped motor protection.

tests.bedienen: Start and stop on the panel

25-rolltor.title: Existing plant: roller door hall 2
25-rolltor.mail.subject: Our roller door does whatever it wants
25-rolltor.mail.body:
Hello,

the roller door in hall 2 was programmed by a company that no longer exists. Since then there's trouble: if someone presses “close” while it's going up, the motor hums in both directions, the warning lamp only flashes when going down, and the maintenance counter shows fantasy values.

The program is attached – please repair it, but don't rewrite it: the plant has been accepted and we have to document every change. The less you change, the better.

Regards
Bernd Wallner
25-rolltor.datasheet:
# Roller door hall 2

**Existing plant:** hardware and program are supplied. Find the faults and change as little as possible – the **amount of change** is scored as well (changed program lines; blank and comment lines don't count). “Discard solution” restores the supplied state.

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | DI | Button open |
| S2 | DI | Button close |
| B1 | DI | End position up |
| B2 | DI | End position down (roller switch, **bounces** for up to 50 ms) |
| B3 | DI | Light barrier, normally closed: 1 = clear |
| M1 | DO | Motor open |
| M2 | DO | Motor close |
| H1 | DO | Warning lamp |

## Required function

1. Open (S1) moves the door to the upper end position, close (S2) to the lower end position.
2. **Never both motors at the same time.** The button for the opposite direction is ignored while moving.
3. Light barrier interrupted while closing: stop immediately and open again.
4. The **warning lamp** is lit while the door moves – in both directions.
5. `"Tor".zyklen` counts the **closing operations** (arrival in the lower end position), exactly once per operation.

## Timing

Tolerance ± 50 ms per switching edge.

## Notes

- The compiler warns when a variable is written in several places.
- Against bouncing switches the module's **input delay** helps (control cabinet: click the module) – a configuration change does not count as a program change.

26-saege.title: Extension: cut on the cross-cut saw
26-saege.mail.subject: The stop works – now the saw, please
26-saege.mail.body:
Hello,

since your modification the stop moves to the millimetre. Now the saw should be added: clamp, blade down, back up, release – all at the push of a button.

Important: nothing may change about the stop, it runs as it is. And while sawing, the stop must under no circumstances move.

Regards
Martin Stöckl
26-saege.datasheet:
# Cross-cut saw – extension cut

**Extension:** you start with your solution of job 23 (or, if there is none, with the supplied one). Its tests keep running as **regression tests** and must still pass.

## New field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| S2 | DI | Button cut |
| B3 | DI | Saw down |
| B4 | DI | Saw up |
| Y1 | DO | Clamping cylinder |
| M3 | DO | Saw down (blade running) |
| M4 | DO | Saw up |

The existing output module is full – plan a second one.

## Cut

1. Rising edge at S2 while the stop is standing and no cut is running: **Y1 on**.
2. **300 ms** later (clamping time): **M3 on** until B3 (saw down).
3. Then **M4 on** until B4 (saw up).
4. Then **Y1 off** – the cut is done.

## Interlock

- While a cut is running, the stop doesn't move; a start during this time is not stored.
- M3 and M4 never at the same time.

## Timing

Tolerance ± 50 ms per switching edge.

tests.alt_drei: Regression: Three boards in a row

checks.Anschlag steht während des Schnitts: Stop stands still during the cut
checks.Säge nie gleichzeitig ab und auf: Saw never down and up at the same time

27-hochbehaelter.title: Masterpiece: high-level tank
27-hochbehaelter.mail.subject: To finish: our high-level tank
27-hochbehaelter.mail.body:
Hello,

we were told you have controlled pretty much everything that moves by now. So to finish, something a whole municipality depends on: our high-level tank.

The pump should hold the level, the attendant wants to switch automatic mode on and off at the panel and see what's going on. And if the measurement fails, the pump must not keep running blindly – then an alarm should appear.

Once that works, you have our thanks – and a place on the wall of former apprentices.

Claudia Altmann
27-hochbehaelter.datasheet:
# High-level tank Altenstein

## Field devices

| Device | Kind | Description |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | AI | Level 0 … 100 %, signal **4–20 mA** |
| P1 | DO | Feed pump (power: relay output) |
| P2 | Panel | Switch automatic |
| P3 | Panel | Lamp pump running |
| P4 | Panel | Lamp measurement faulty |

## Function

1. **Automatic** (P2 on): pump on below **40 %**, off above **80 %** (hysteresis).
2. Automatic off: pump off.
3. **Measurement faulty** (wire break at the sensor): pump off, P4 on, an **alarm** (Program_Alarm) is active. Once the measurement is back, normal operation continues.
4. P3 shows whether the pump is running.
5. Level always between **35 % and 85 %** in operation, the pump switches at most 10 times in 40 s.

## Notes

- The sensor delivers 4–20 mA: set the analog module's measuring range accordingly. On a wire break the channel delivers **32767**.
- The panel is connected via memory bits (tags P_Auto, P_Pumpe, P_Stoerung).
